a.title: Register the breadth book with the screen as a hard gate
a.means: the confirmatory run passes --require-screen research/breadth/screen/screen_multi7.json; every candidate failed or was not screened, so the run refuses before reading any data (breadth_book.screen_check, WriteBroker.preregister(screen=)). Expected outcome: no confirmatory look - a documented negative result (no registered equity alpha clears spread + fee + impact at one round lot on multi7). The holdout stays unread and unspent.
a.ledger: the registration debits one look of kind prereg; the refused run reads nothing and debits nothing

b.title: Register a named candidate with a screen override
b.why_this_one: best reading on the screen's pre-registered gate statistic (net day-clustered t) among the candidates the book can run: the book's scores are eq11 (EQ11/15m, not screened: no scored row on three names) and eq10_beta_gap (EQ10/1s). Screen-wide, the best net day-clustered t is EQ09/10s/linear_z_v1 (-8.93), which has no book score; registering it would need a new score, i.e. new code under a new fingerprint.
b.means: the confirmatory run omits --require-screen and records the screen status (fail) on its report; the override is a ledger entry of its own, stating the screen path, sha256, the candidate's FAIL status and the owner's reason, written at registration. The prior from the screen is strongly negative: the candidate loses about 1.97 bps per round trip net at one lot on the in-sample days.
b.ledger: one look of kind prereg plus one override entry; the confirmatory run debits one breadth_book look on the holdout dataset

c.title: Defer C8 to v1.18 pending new candidates
c.means: no registration in v1.17; v1.17 ships the in-sample book (plan section 7 fallback). New candidates come from screening the 100-name breadth day(s) (data/real/breadth, in-sample 2019/20 only) or a different registered size; C8 is redrafted against that screen. The holdout stays unread and unspent.

hypothesis: On the breadth holdout (the 2025/26 Nasdaq days, names of the fixed breadth universe outside AAPL / MSFT / QQQ), the cross-sectional book driven by the registered score, through the cost-aware optimizer at the registered notional, earns a mean daily net P&L (gross minus spread, fee and impact) whose day-clustered t is at least 2.0 with a positive mean per-rebalance rank IC; and its deflated Sharpe at the registered N is at least 0.95. Anything less is a negative result, recorded as such.
